community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body
size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender
identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status,
nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual
identity and orientation.

## Our Standards

Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment:

- Using welcoming and inclusive language
- Being respectful of differing viewpoints and experiences
- Gracefully accepting constructive criticism
- Focusing on what is best for the community
- Showing empathy towards other community members

Examples of unacceptable behavior:

- Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
- Public or private harassment
- Publishing others' private information without explicit permission
- Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate

## Enforcement

Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be
reported by opening an issue or contacting the maintainer directly.

# Contributing

Thanks for your interest in StickySites.

## Getting started

See [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) for setup instructions, commands,
and coding conventions.

## Pull requests

1. Fork the repo and create a feature branch
2. Make your changes, following the conventions in DEVELOPMENT.md
3. Run `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run test:peer`, and both documentation checks; see DEVELOPMENT.md for safe integration fixtures
4. Submit a PR using the [PR template](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md)

## Code style

- Vanilla JS only — no frameworks, transpilers, or bundlers
- Content scripts use `window.StickySites` namespace (no ES modules)
- All DOM elements use `stickysites-` prefix
- Storage keys are versioned with `_v1` suffix
- 2-space indentation, LF line endings (enforced by .editorconfig)

## Source: PRIVACY.md

# StickySites Privacy Policy

_Last updated: 2026-11-12_

StickySites keeps notes attached to websites, pages, and dates, plus a to-do list and an
outliner. Notes are stored locally by default. We operate no hosted collection service,
analytics, telemetry, crash reporting, or advertising. Optional sync sends data only through
the local programs, paired computers, and shared/cloud folder you choose.

## What the extension stores

- Notes, to-do items, outlines, deletion markers, sync status, and your settings.
- If encryption is enabled: a random salt, an encrypted verification token, and a cached
  derived key while unlocked. The passphrase itself is never stored.

The extension uses `chrome.storage.local`, not Chrome's account-sync storage. The cached
key deliberately persists across browser restarts until **Lock Now**. Other extensions do
not have direct access to this extension's storage. An open in-page note panel is part of
the host page's DOM: that page's scripts can read its displayed plaintext. Encryption at
rest does not hide content while you display it on a page.

## What the extension reads from web pages

- Hostname and path identify the site/page note and its icon.
- Selected text is read when you explicitly choose a StickySites clipping menu item.

StickySites does not automatically scrape page content. Imported rich-text HTML is filtered
before display to remove scripts, event attributes, embedded resource nodes, and unsafe URLs.

## Network and optional sync

The extension loads no remote code or resources and sends no hosted telemetry. It can call
an optional helper on `127.0.0.1`. That helper can exchange snapshots over a paired LAN or
write them to your chosen shared/cloud folder. These optional boundaries are described below.

### Local to-do sync

If you install the optional native-messaging host, the extension sends to-do item text,
done state, notes, sections, and identifiers to that local program so it can synchronize a
Markdown file. The extension skips this sync while the vault is enabled or the to-do value
is encrypted. The extension itself does not upload that file; a folder synchronization
service you independently use may transfer it under that service's terms.

### Paired LAN sync

If you enable peer sync and install `peer/stickysites-peer.py`, the extension passes a
snapshot to its local helper over loopback. Helpers authenticate discovery with a shared
pairing key and exchange snapshots over HTTPS with certificate fingerprints pinned from
those signed announcements. The helper stores the latest snapshot on your computer.
Without the helper, peer sync is unavailable; it can be switched off in Settings.

### Shared or cloud folder

You may configure a sync folder, including a network share or a Google Drive, iCloud Drive,
or Dropbox folder. Each helper writes a signed snapshot file there and reads paired peers'
files. Your chosen provider may store and transfer those files outside your device or LAN,
under its own terms. StickySites does not operate that provider or receive those files.
Clear the folder setting to stop future writes; delete existing copies separately.

## Encryption

Encryption is optional: AES-256-GCM with PBKDF2-SHA256 and 600,000 iterations derives a key
from your passphrase. With the vault enabled, the six note buckets travel as encrypted
envelopes. Deletion markers (including record keys and timestamps), crypto configuration,
device names/identifiers, and folder-signature metadata remain readable. With encryption
off, snapshots and shared-folder files contain plaintext notes. Folder signatures authenticate
a file; they do not encrypt it. We cannot recover a forgotten passphrase.

## Data sharing and sale

We do not collect or sell your personal data. Optional transfers occur through the local
host, paired computers, or folder provider you select. Notes and settings serve only the
extension's note-taking and synchronization features.

## Permissions

| Permission | Why it is needed |
|---|---|
| `storage` | Save notes, settings, vault configuration, and sync state locally |
| `activeTab` | Open or toggle a note panel on the active tab |
| `contextMenus` | Offer the explicit clipping menu |
| `alarms` | Schedule optional to-do and peer sync |
| `nativeMessaging` | Talk to the optional local to-do program |
| Content script on websites | Display the floating cluster and panel |

## Removing your data

Export readable notes as Markdown before uninstalling. Removing the extension deletes its
Chrome extension storage. It does not delete the helper's state, local Markdown file,
paired computers' copies, or shared/cloud-folder files; remove those separately if desired.

## Changes and contact

Policy updates appear at https://github.com/mithudso/stickysites/blob/main/PRIVACY.md with a
new date. Contact the maintainer through https://github.com/mithudso/stickysites/issues.

## Source: README.md

# StickySites

[![CI](https://github.com/mithudso/stickysites/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mithudso/stickysites/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Sticky notes for every website. A Chrome Extension (Manifest V3) with six note
types, a floating draggable icon cluster, a rich-text workspace panel with find & replace and
@-mention autocomplete, a full to-do list that can sync with a local `TODO.md`, a global
outliner library, opt-in AES-256-GCM encryption at rest, and optional peer-to-peer sync between
your own laptops over a paired LAN or a shared folder you choose. No hosted service or telemetry.

## Note types

| Color  | Type        | Scope |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| Yellow | Global      | One shared note, visible on every site |
| Green  | Site        | One note per domain |
| Blue   | Page        | One note per exact URL path |
| Purple | To-do list  | One global checklist with sections, priorities, tags, colors |
| Orange | Outliner    | Global library of named hierarchical outlines |
| Red    | Daily       | One note per calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) |

## Features

### Floating icon cluster
- Draggable pill with one identity-bearing icon per note type (🌐, domain fragment, path
  segment, day of month); long-press to reorder; horizontal or vertical layout
- **Alt+S** shows/hides the cluster; **Ctrl/Cmd+F1…F6** open Global, Site, Page, To-do,
  Outline, Daily (toggle: same key closes, another key switches)
- Icons and open site/page notes follow SPA navigation automatically

### Workspace panel
- Move by the header; resize from any edge or corner; expand/shrink toggle
- **Pop out** to a standalone window with the ⧉ button — or drag the panel off the page
- Rich text editor with a 19-tool toolbar (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, H1–H3,
  lists, checkbox, alignment, rule, indent/outdent, font family, font size, color)
- **Find & Replace** (`Cmd/Ctrl+F` / `Cmd/Ctrl+H`) with match counter and Replace All
- `@` mentions: links, dates, contacts, files; inline `#tags`; auto-save after 500 ms
- Live cross-tab sync — edits in one tab appear in every other open panel

### To-do list
- Nested items (Tab/Shift+Tab), sections, priority 0–5, color swatches, tags, per-item notes,
  drag-to-reorder, completed timestamps
- Optional two-way sync with a local `TODO.md` through a native-messaging host
  (`docs/external-calls.md`); works fully offline without it

### Outliner
- Library of named outline documents with a switcher; New / Rename / Duplicate / Delete
- Keyboard-first: Enter, Tab/Shift+Tab, Alt+↑/↓, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter to complete
- Zoom into any node (breadcrumb back), collapse, per-node notes, `#tag` chips, filter,
  heuristic Auto-group with Undo, export to Markdown or OPML

### Context menu
- Right-click selected text → **StickySites** → clip into any of the six note types

### Popup
- Quick-Open row (one button per note type), full-text search, sort (Recent / Oldest / A–Z),
  type and tag filters, Markdown export
- Settings: encryption Enable / Disable / **Lock Now**, note-type visibility, cluster layout

### Local peer sync (optional)
- Keep two or more of your laptops converged over the local network, or through your own shared/cloud folder
- A tiny stdlib-Python helper on each machine discovers peers (multicast + subnet broadcast, pairing key) and relays
  snapshots over pinned TLS; merging is record-level last-writer-wins inside the extension
- Encrypted vaults sync as envelopes; enable encryption on one laptop and the others adopt it
- Setup: `python3 peer/stickysites-peer.py install`, then paste the pairing key (and, if your
  network blocks discovery, the other laptop's IP) in the popup Settings — see [peer/README.md](peer/README.md)

### Encryption at rest
- Opt-in AES-256-GCM; key derived from your passphrase with PBKDF2 (600,000 iterations, SHA-256)
- The derived key is cached locally until you click **Lock Now**; an in-page lock overlay
  asks for the passphrase when locked. There is no passphrase recovery — see
  `docs/runbooks/encryption-lock-and-recovery.md`

## Quick start

1. Clone this repository
2. Open `chrome://extensions`, enable **Developer mode**
3. **Load unpacked** → select the repo root
4. Visit any page: click a cluster icon, or press **Ctrl/Cmd+F1**

Full details: [docs/INSTALLATION.md](docs/INSTALLATION.md).

## Development

```bash
npm ci                      # development dependencies from the lockfile
npm run lint                # syntax, ESLint, and version agreement
npm test                    # pure modules and actual-script DOM regressions
npm run test:peer            # synthetic actual-daemon tests on loopback
npm run docs:check-generated # verify generated public documentation matches sources
```

No build step — Chrome loads the repo root directly. Use the Node version in `.nvmrc` that satisfies `package.json` for the tooling.
See [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) and [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md).

## Tech stack

- Chrome Extension Manifest V3 (content scripts + module service worker)
- Vanilla JavaScript and CSS — no frameworks, transpilers, or bundlers
- Web Crypto API (PBKDF2, AES-256-GCM)
- Vitest with jsdom for runtime regression tests; optional puppeteer-core browser harnesses

## Source: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

# Architecture

## Overview

StickySites is a Chrome Extension (Manifest V3) that injects a floating note workspace into
every web page. Notes live in `chrome.storage.local` with optional AES-256-GCM encryption.
There is no hosted StickySites service or telemetry. Optional native messaging mirrors
to-dos into `TODO.md`. An optional loopback daemon relays snapshots to paired LAN computers
or to a shared/cloud folder selected by the user.

## System context

```
  User ──▶ Chrome
            ├─ Content scripts (per tab; classic scripts in manifest order)
            │    Cluster pill · Panel (rich text / to-do / outliner) · lock overlay · toast
            │    reads storage; mutations ──▶ service-worker write queue
            ├─ Service worker (ES module)
            │    menus · commands · popout · sync · note-writer queue → chrome.storage.local
            │    ──▶ chrome.runtime.sendNativeMessage('com.mitch.todo_bridge')  (optional)
            │    │     └─▶ ~/.claude/skills/todo/scripts/todo_host ⇄ TODO.md
            │    ──▶ fetch http://127.0.0.1:47831  (optional peer daemon, peer/stickysites-peer.py)
            │          ├─▶ LAN: signed discovery + pinned HTTPS ⇄ paired daemons
            │          └─▶ selected shared/cloud folder ⇄ paired snapshot files
            ├─ Popup page (popup.html)   Quick-Open · search · settings · lock screen
            └─ Popout page (popout.html) Panel filling its own window
```

External actors: the user; the host web page (untrusted DOM the UI is injected into); the
optional native host process; the optional peer daemon and, through it, the user's other
machines holding the same pairing key, plus any folder provider the user chooses.

## Runtime contexts and communication

| Context | File(s) | Module system | Talks to |
|---|---|---|---|
| Content scripts | `src/content/*.js` | classic, `window.StickySites.*` | storage reads; SW via `STICKYSITES_WRITE` / `POPOUT` / `UNLOCK`; receives `TOGGLE` / `OPEN` / `CLIP` |
| Service worker | `src/background/service-worker.js` | ES module (`note-writer.js`, sync/crypto modules, shared classic helpers) | tabs via `tabs.sendMessage`; native host; `windows.create`; loopback `fetch` to the peer daemon |
| Popup | `popup.html` + shared classic helpers + `popup.js` | classic `<script>` | storage reads; queued mutations; active tab via `tabs.sendMessage(OPEN/TOGGLE)`; SW via `POPOUT` |
| Popout | `popout.html` + namespace helpers + `popout.js` | classic `<script>` | storage reads; queued mutations via SW |
| Tests | `tests/*.test.js` | Vitest, node/jsdom | synthetic storage, IPC, fetch, and native calls |

## Data flows

1. **Page load** — content scripts run at `document_idle`. `sticky-inject.js` exits if
   `#stickysites-cluster` already exists, else initialises `Panel` and `Cluster` from prefs.
2. **Open a note** — cluster icon click, `Ctrl/Cmd+F1…F6`, popup Quick-Open (`STICKYSITES_OPEN`),
   or a clip. `checkUnlocked()` first: if encryption is enabled and no cached key, the lock
   overlay is shown instead. `Panel.open(type)` snapshots `_activeKey`/`_activeLabel`, reads
   and decrypts the record, renders the right editor. The notice opens a fixed extension-origin
   unlock window; the host page has no passphrase input.
3. **Edit** — rich text (`contenteditable` + `execCommand`), to-do list, or outliner. Every
   change arms a 500 ms debounce; the write encrypts when a key is cached. `flushPendingSave()`
   commits early on close, switch, popout, or SPA re-key. Mutations enter the single SW
   queue, read fresh records, and verify persistence. A deletion and its tombstone share a write.
4. **Cross-tab sync** — `chrome.storage.onChanged` in every tab → `Panel.syncFromStorage`.
   Guards: self-echo (skip the body this panel just wrote), focus (never rewrite a focused
   editor, re-checked after async decryption), dirty/in-flight saves, encryption (skip while locked).
5. **SPA navigation** — `popstate`, `hashchange`, and a 1 s `href` poll. On change: flush the
   pending save under the old key, `Cluster.refreshIcons()`, re-open an open site/page note
   under the new key.
6. **Clip** — right-click selection → SW `contextMenus.onClicked` → `STICKYSITES_CLIP` →
   a queued clip command appends escaped text to a fresh target record and shows a toast.
7. **Popout** — ⧉ button or drag-off-page → `Panel._popoutActiveNote()` → flush →
   `STICKYSITES_POPOUT` → SW `windows.create(popout.html?type&key&label, 1400×1100)`.
   `popout.js` overrides `getKey/getLabel` on a cloned note type and opens the panel.
8. **To-do sync** — SW runs `syncTodosWithHost` on startup/install, every 2 min (alarm), and
   3 s after `stickysites_todos_v1` changes. Skipped while the vault is enabled or the value is an encrypted envelope.
   The host three-way-merges with `TODO.md`; `applyHostResult` folds the reply back while
   keeping StickySites-only fields. A guarded commit rejects the reply with `STATE_CHANGED`
   if the to-do or vault changed while the host was working.
9. **Local peer sync** — SW runs `syncWithDaemon` on startup/install, every minute (alarm),
   4 s after a note/tombstone/crypto change, and on `STICKYSITES_PEER_SYNC_NOW`. It `PUT`s a
   snapshot (six note keys as stored + tombstones + reduced vault config) to
   `http://127.0.0.1:47831`, `GET`s peer snapshots from LAN or the selected folder, merges
   record-level last-writer-wins on `updatedAt` (decrypting/re-encrypting with the cached key
   when the vault is on and salts match), and guarded-commits changed keys only if the inputs
   remain current. No daemon → one warning, no-op.
10. **Encryption lifecycle** — popup Settings → `Crypto.enable(passphrase)` derives the key,
   stages every encrypted bucket, config, and cached JWK before one guarded multi-key write.
   Disable stages every decryption first, so a corrupt bucket preserves the vault for recovery.
   **Lock Now** clears the cached key; unlock re-derives and verifies. The JWK otherwise
   remains in `chrome.storage.local` across browser restarts. Content pages without secure-context
   WebCrypto use extension-worker vault IPC with the same lifecycle and storage protocol.

## Content script load order

| Order | File | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| First | `src/shared/settings.js`, `src/shared/network.js` | Preference normalization and bounded requests |
| Then | `storage-content.js`, `safe-html.js`, `crypto-content.js` | Mutation IPC, inert HTML filtering, vault operations |
| Then | `note-types.js`, `prefs.js`, `cluster.js`, `todo.js`, `outline-ops.js` | Descriptors, preferences, and UI primitives |
| Last | `outline.js`, `mentions.js`, `panel.js`, `sticky-inject.js` | Editors and orchestration |

`manifest.json` is the exact ordered source of truth. Extension-page script lists live in
`popup.html` and `popout.html`; they also load the shared mutation and safety helpers.

## Storage schema (`chrome.storage.local`)

Encrypted note values are replaced wholesale by `{ iv: base64, data: base64 }` envelopes.

| Key | Shape |
|-----|-------|
| `stickysites_global_v1` | `{ body, updatedAt }` |
| `stickysites_sites_v1` | `{ [hostname]: { key, label, body, tags[], createdAt, updatedAt } }` (legacy `siteKey`/`siteLabel`) |
| `stickysites_pages_v1` | `{ [origin+pathname]: { key, label, body, tags[], createdAt, updatedAt } }` (legacy `pageKey`/`pageLabel`) |
| `stickysites_todos_v1` | `{ __global__: { key, items[], sections[], tagColors, createdAt, updatedAt } }` |
| `stickysites_outlines_v1` | `{ [ol_<id>]: { key, name, items[], createdAt, updatedAt } }` (legacy hostname keys adapt at read) |
| `stickysites_daily_v1` | `{ [YYYY-MM-DD]: { key, body, ... } }` |
| `stickysites_prefs_v1` | `{ clusterPosition {x,y}, clusterLayout, collapseToCircle, iconOrder, enabledTypes, panelSize, panelPosition, activeOutlineId, panelMode (unused) }` |
| `stickysites_crypto_v1` | `{ enabled, salt: base64, verify: envelope }` |
| `stickysites_cached_key` | JWK of the derived AES-GCM key while unlocked; null/absent while locked |
| `stickysites_tombstones_v1` | `{ [storageKey]: { [recordKey]: deletedAtISO } }` — deletions to propagate via peer sync (plaintext) |
| `stickysites_peer_v1` | `{ deviceId, enabled, lastSync, lastResult: { status, peers[], changedKeys[], stats } }` |

**Todo item**: `{ id, text, done, indent 0–3, priority 0–5, color, tags[], note, section, completedAt }`.
**Outline node**: `{ id, text, children[], collapsed, note, done, tags[] }`.

`chrome.storage.session` is not used (an earlier design cached the key there; the dead
`setAccessLevel` call was removed in v1.11.1).

## Permissions

| Permission | Why |
|------------|-----|
| `storage` | All persistence |
| `activeTab` | `tabs.sendMessage` / `tabs.query` for the active tab |
| `contextMenus` | The "StickySites" clip submenu |
| `alarms` | To-do and peer sync schedules (service workers cannot retain timers) |
| `nativeMessaging` | `runtime.sendNativeMessage` to `com.mitch.todo_bridge` |

Content scripts match `<all_urls>` at `document_idle`.

## Design decisions (ADRs)

### ADR-1 Namespace pattern for content scripts
MV3 content scripts cannot `import`. Every module attaches to `window.StickySites` and the
manifest lists them in dependency order. Consequence: `popout.html` must repeat the list;
`crypto.js` (ES) duplicates `crypto-content.js` (namespace) for the worker and tests.
Portable `settings.js` and `network.js` classic helpers also run in the module worker.

### ADR-2 IIFE guard against double injection
`sticky-inject.js` returns if `#stickysites-cluster` exists, so re-injection after an
extension update cannot build a second UI (orphaned listeners remain — `known-issues.md`).

### ADR-3 Cached key lives in `chrome.storage.local` until Lock Now
The derived key's JWK persists across browser restarts instead of dying with a session.
Consequence: one passphrase entry per explicit lock rather than per session; the JWK sits in
the profile directory while unlocked (`docs/SECURITY.md`). An earlier design used
`chrome.storage.session`; docs and code were reconciled in v1.11.1.

### ADR-4 Snapshot the note key at `open()`
The panel never re-derives its key mid-session; SPA navigation re-keys by flushing and
re-opening. This closed a class of "saved under the wrong page" bugs.

### ADR-5 Outliner is a global library, not site-keyed
Outline docs are `ol_<id>` records with names; the active doc is a pref. Legacy hostname keys
adapt at read time. Consequence: `noteType.getKey` returns `''` and the renderer resolves the doc.

### ADR-6 No bare-key hotkeys
Bare `1`–`5`/`A` shortcuts hijacked typing and `Cmd+A`; only `Alt+S` and `Ctrl/Cmd+F1…F6` remain.

### ADR-7 The native host owns the to-do merge
The extension sends its full list and accepts the host's result; it adds nothing but
StickySites-only fields. Consequence: merge rules live in one place (`todo.py`), and the
extension needs no file access. Sync is skipped for encrypted data so plaintext never reaches disk.

### ADR-9 Peer sync through a local relay daemon, merge in the extension
Extensions cannot listen on sockets or do multicast, so a stdlib-Python daemon per machine handles
discovery (UDP multicast plus subnet broadcast on every non-tunnel interface, optional static
peers; HMAC-signed with a shared pairing key) and transport (HTTPS, pinned
self-signed cert, bearer token). The daemon only stores and relays opaque snapshots; the merge
(record-level LWW + tombstones, vault-aware) lives in `src/shared/peer-sync.js` where it is
unit-tested. The extension reaches the daemon with a CORS-gated loopback `fetch`, so no manifest
permission was added. Consequence: snapshots are full-state each minute (fine at note scale);
deletions need tombstones (only outline docs delete today).

### ADR-8 Read-time schema adaptation instead of migrations
Legacy field names and keys are normalised when read. Storage keys are versioned (`_v1`)
so a breaking change can still ship as a new key.

## Source: docs/COMPONENTS.md

# Components

"Namespace" = the `window.StickySites.*` object a classic content
script attaches; "Exports" = ES module exports.

## Service worker — `src/background/service-worker.js` (ES module)

Imports the `note-writer.js` mutation queue, shared settings/network helpers, `todo-bridge.js` (to-do sync), `peer-sync.js` (LAN sync), `crypto.js` (`importJwk`, `encrypt`, `decrypt` for the peer merge).

| Responsibility | Detail |
|---|---|
| Context menus | `onInstalled`: parent `stickysites-parent` (selection context) + children `clip-global/site/page/todo/outline/daily`; `onClicked` → `tabs.sendMessage(STICKYSITES_CLIP)` |
| Command | `toggle-cluster` (`Alt+S`) → `STICKYSITES_TOGGLE` to the active tab |
| Popout | `onMessage(STICKYSITES_POPOUT)` → `windows.create(popout.html?type&key&label, popup, 1400×1100)` |
| To-do sync | `runTodoSync()` with a `todoSyncRunning` guard; alarm `stickysites-todo-sync` every 2 min; `onStartup`, `onInstalled`; 3 s after `storage.onChanged` touches `stickysites_todos_v1` |
| Peer sync | `runPeerSync()` with a `peerSyncRunning` guard; alarm `stickysites-peer-sync` every 1 min; `onStartup`, `onInstalled`; 4 s after a note / tombstone / crypto change or the enable toggle; `STICKYSITES_PEER_SYNC_NOW` from the popup replies with the persisted state. `peerCryptoApi()` turns the cached JWK into `{ decrypt, encrypt }` for the merge |
| Mutation IPC | `STICKYSITES_WRITE` dispatches record, clip, preference, lock, and guarded commits to one queue; writes use fresh reads and read-back verification |
| Failure paths | `console.warn('[stickysites] …')` when a tab has no content script, the native host fails, or the peer daemon errors (the "no daemon" case is logged once per outage) |

---

## Shared runtime safety helpers

- `src/shared/settings.js`: portable classic `StickySites.Settings` with normalized prefs and timeout defaults.
- `src/shared/network.js`: portable classic `StickySites.request`; its deadline includes JSON body consumption.
- `src/content/storage-content.js`: `STICKYSITES_WRITE` IPC to the service worker.
- `src/shared/note-writer.js`: sole runtime mutation queue, fresh record reads, guarded commits, and persisted-value verification. `STATE_CHANGED` rejects stale native/peer results.
- `src/content/safe-html.js`: inert HTML parsing and allowlist filtering before live rendering; `Html.text` produces plain export/search text.

## `src/content/crypto-content.js` — `StickySites.Crypto`

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `generateSalt()` | 16 random bytes |
| `deriveKey(passphrase, salt)` | PBKDF2-SHA256 × 600,000 → AES-GCM-256 `CryptoKey` (extractable, so it can be cached as JWK) |
| `encrypt(key, text)` / `decrypt(key, envelope)` | 12-byte IV; `{ iv, data }` base64 envelope |
| `isEncrypted(v)` | string `iv` + `data`, and no `body` / `items` / `siteKey` |
| `isEnabled()` / `getConfig()` | Read `stickysites_crypto_v1` |
| `cacheKey(key)` / `getCachedKey()` / `clearCachedKey()` | JWK in `chrome.storage.local["stickysites_cached_key"]` plus invalidated per-context cache; cleared to null on lock |
| `enable(passphrase)` | Stage every note bucket plus salt/verify/config/JWK, then guarded commit |
| `unlock(passphrase)` | Derive, check against `verify`, cache; returns boolean |
| `disable()` | Stage every decryption before committing note buckets and cleared config/key; corrupt buckets preserve the existing vault |
| `encryptValue(v)` / `decryptValue(v)` | Encryption refuses missing keys; decryption preserves unreadable/locked envelopes |

Storage: `stickysites_crypto_v1`, `stickysites_cached_key`, the six note keys.

## `src/content/note-types.js` — `StickySites.noteTypes` (array of 6)

Each descriptor: `id, color, tint, tintText, label, emoji, cssClass, storageKey,
storagePattern, getKey(location), getLabel(location), getPlaceholder()`; site/page/daily add
`getIconContent()` / `getIconTitle()` (first 4 domain chars · last path segment (3 chars + …) ·
day of month).

| id | storageKey | pattern | getKey |
|---|---|---|---|
| global | `stickysites_global_v1` | single | `'__global__'` |
| site | `stickysites_sites_v1` | map | hostname without `www.` |
| page | `stickysites_pages_v1` | map | origin + pathname |
| todo | `stickysites_todos_v1` | structured | `'__global__'` |
| outline | `stickysites_outlines_v1` | structured | `''` (renderer resolves the doc) |
| daily | `stickysites_daily_v1` | map | `YYYY-MM-DD` |

## `src/content/prefs.js` — `StickySites.Prefs`

`read()` → defaults merged with `stickysites_prefs_v1`; `write(updates)` → shallow merge, returns
merged prefs or `null`. Writes use queued mutation IPC and the shared normalizer in `settings.js`. Defaults: `clusterPosition {x:null,y:null}`, `panelMode 'fixed'`
(unused), `clusterLayout 'vertical'`, `iconOrder null`, `enabledTypes` (all six true),
`panelSize null`, `panelPosition null`. `activeOutlineId` is written by `outline.js` /
`sticky-inject.js` without a default.

## `src/content/cluster.js` — `StickySites.Cluster`

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `init(noteTypes, onIconClick)` | Build icons in `iconOrder`, apply `clusterLayout`, `clusterPosition`, `enabledTypes`; wire drag + long-press (400 ms) reorder |
| `setActive(typeId)` | Toggle `is-active` |
| `refreshIcons()` | Recompute identity icon text/titles (called on SPA navigation) |
| `getVisibleIcons()` / `getVisibleTypeIds()` | Icons not `display:none` |
| `toggle()` | Hide/show; on hide deactivates and calls `onIconClick(null)` |
| `applyLayout(layout)` | Toggle `is-horizontal` live (popup settings) |

Writes prefs `iconOrder`, `clusterPosition`. DOM: `#stickysites-cluster`, `.stickysites-cluster-icon`.

## `src/content/todo.js` — `StickySites.Todo`

`COLORS` (8 swatches), `PRIORITY_COLORS` (1–5), `genId()`, `normalizeItem(item)` →
`{ id, text, done, indent 0–3, priority 0–5, color, tags, note, section, completedAt }`,
`normalizeData(note)` → `{ items, sections, tagColors }`,
`DragController.init(listEl, getItems, getSections, onReorder)` — grip drag with a drop
indicator; the dropped item adopts the target's section.

## `src/content/outline-ops.js` — `StickySites.OutlineOps` (pure; unit-tested)

`genId`, `normalizeNode/normalizeItems`, `findParent(id, arr)` → `{ parent, array, index }`,
`findNode`, `getPathTo`, `insertSiblingAfter`, `indentNode`, `outdentNode`, `moveNode(items, id, ±1)`,
`removeNode` (promotes children), `extractTags`, `filterTree(items, q)` (matches + ancestors,
`null` when empty), `autoGroup` (by first tag → shared keyword → "Other"), `toMarkdown`
(`~~done~~`), `toOPML(items, name)` (OPML 2.0 with `_note`, `_complete`).

## `src/content/outline.js` — `StickySites.Outline`

| Member | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `readLibrary()` | Decrypt `stickysites_outlines_v1` → `{ map, docs }` sorted by `updatedAt` desc; legacy hostname keys adapt |
| `writeDoc(key, name, items)` | Upsert; returns `null` (refuses) while locked |
| `newDocKey()` | `ol_<id>` |
| `render(panel, noteType, explicitKey)` | Resolve doc (explicit key → `getKey` → `activeOutlineId` → first doc → create "My outline"); build switcher, toolbar, ⋯ menu (New / Rename / Duplicate / Delete / Auto-group + 10 s Undo / Export Markdown / Export OPML), breadcrumb, list, filter |

Keyboard on a node input: Enter (sibling), Ctrl/Cmd+Enter (done), Tab / Shift+Tab (indent /
outdent, never above the zoom root), Alt+↑/↓ (move), ↑/↓ (focus), Backspace on empty (delete),
Esc (blur). Prefs: reads/writes `activeOutlineId`. Shows `.stickysites-outline-locked` while locked.

## `src/content/mentions.js` — `StickySites.Mentions`

`attach(editorEl)` watches for `@`, `show()` / `hide()`. Categories Link (paste URL, current
page URL), Date (today, tomorrow, this week, pick), Contact (name, email), File. Dropdown
`#stickysites-mentions` positioned at the caret; ↑/↓, Enter/Tab select, Esc; inserts
`.stickysites-mention-chip`. Uses `prompt()` for free-text input.

## `src/content/panel.js` — `StickySites.Panel`

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `init(onClose)` | Create `#stickysites-panel`; drag (header) and 8-grip resize (`_initResize` pins to absolute left/top); drag-off-page popout hint within 28 px of an edge |
| `open(noteType)` | Flush pending save → snapshot `_activeKey` / `_activeLabel` → `_readNote` (decrypt) → `_render` / `_renderTodo` / `Outline.render` → apply `panelSize` / `panelPosition` |
| `close()` | Flush, tear down |
| `flushPendingSave()` | Run an armed debounce immediately |
| `syncFromStorage(changes)` | Rich-text types only; self-echo, focus, encryption guards |
| `_popoutActiveNote()` | Flush → `runtime.sendMessage(STICKYSITES_POPOUT)` |
| `_buildToolbar()` | 19 controls: 16 buttons + font family (5) + font size (4) + color |
| `_readNote` / `_writeNote` / `_writeStructured` | Queued record mutations with encryption; loaded item ids preserve additions from other writers |
| `_toggleExpand()` | 900 px wide; min size 350×250 |

Find & Replace: `Cmd/Ctrl+F` / `Cmd/Ctrl+H` toggle the bar; Enter / Shift+Enter next / prev;
Esc closes; `<mark>` highlights stripped by `getCleanHtml()` before save. To-do input keys:
Enter (new), Tab / Shift+Tab (indent 0–3), Backspace on empty (delete), Esc (blur); tag input
Enter adds a tag. Opening the to-do panel focuses the first empty task (creating one if needed).
Prefs written: `panelPosition`, `panelSize`.

## `src/content/sticky-inject.js` — orchestrator IIFE

Exits if `#stickysites-cluster` exists. Functions: `findNoteType`, `checkUnlocked`,
`showLockOverlay` (`#stickysites-lock`, Enter unlocks), `handleIconClick`, `showToast`
(`#stickysites-toast`), `clipToNote`, `onUrlChange` (`popstate`, `hashchange`, 1 s poll →
`Cluster.refreshIcons()` + re-open site/page note under the new key).
Messages handled: `STICKYSITES_TOGGLE`, `STICKYSITES_OPEN { noteTypeId, key? }`,
`STICKYSITES_CLIP { noteTypeId, text }`. Keyboard: `Ctrl/Cmd+F1…F6` toggle types 0–5
(respecting `enabledTypes`, through the lock check). Forwards `storage.onChanged` to
`Panel.syncFromStorage`.

## `src/content/sticky-inject.css`

All injected styles: cluster, panel, toolbar, find bar, to-do list, outliner, mentions,
lock overlay, toast, popout hint, dark theme, animations. Also linked by `popout.html`.

---

## `src/shared/todo-bridge.js` (ES exports) — used by the SW; unit-tested

| Export | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `TODO_HOST` | `'com.mitch.todo_bridge'` |
| `TODOS_KEY` | `'stickysites_todos_v1'` |
| `buildRequest(record, extId)` | `{ cmd:'sync', ext, items[{id,text,done,note,section}], sections[{id,name}] }` |
| `applyHostResult(record, hostItems)` | Merge host items with local-only fields (indent, priority, color, tags, completedAt); section names ↔ ids; prune empty host-origin sections; `{ items, sections, changed }` via canonical JSON compare |
| `isEncryptedValue(v)` | Same test as `Crypto.isEncrypted` |
| `syncTodosWithHost({ storage, sendNativeMessage, extId, commit })` | Skip while encrypted; bounded native round-trip; guarded commit only when `changed`; returns `{ changed, count }`, `{ skipped }`, or `{ error }` |

## `src/shared/peer-sync.js` (ES exports) — used by the SW; unit-tested

| Export | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `NOTE_KEYS`, `TOMBSTONES_KEY`, `CRYPTO_KEY`, `CACHED_KEY`, `PEER_STATE_KEY`, `DEFAULT_DAEMON_URL` | Constants (`http://127.0.0.1:47831`) |
| `buildSnapshot({ deviceId, notes, tombstones, crypto, ts })` | `{ version:1, deviceId, ts, notes, tombstones, crypto:{enabled,salt}\|null, cryptoFull? }` |
| `recordsOf(storageKey, value)` / `fromRecords(storageKey, records)` | Normalise every note type to `{ recordKey: record }` (global note → `__single__`) and back |
| `cryptoCompatibility(local, remote)` | `compatible` / `adopt-remote` / `remote-off` / `mismatch` |
| `mergeNotes(local, remotes)` | Record-level LWW on `updatedAt` across N peers, tombstone-aware; `{ notes, tombstones, changedKeys, stats }` |
| `syncWithDaemon({ storage, fetch, daemonUrl, cryptoApi, now, commit })` | Full round: read → `PUT /snapshot` → `GET /peers/snapshots` → per-peer vault decision → decrypt → merge → guarded commit of changed keys (re-encrypted when the vault is on) → persist `stickysites_peer_v1` |
| `addTombstone(tombstones, storageKey, recordKey, when)` | Immutable helper for writers that delete records |
| `isEnvelope(v)`, `genDeviceId()` | Helpers |

## `src/shared/crypto.js` (ES exports) — tests + SW

`generateSalt`, `deriveKey` (same PBKDF2/AES-GCM parameters as the namespace version),
`encrypt`, `decrypt`, `importJwk` (cached JWK → `CryptoKey`; used by the SW's peer merge),
`isEncrypted`. Kept in lock-step with `crypto-content.js` (which gained `importJwk` too).

## `peer/stickysites-peer.py` (stdlib Python 3.9+) — local peer daemon

| Piece | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Loopback HTTP `127.0.0.1:47831` | `PUT /snapshot` (stores to `~/.stickysites/snapshot.json`, 0600), `GET /peers/snapshots` (fetches every live peer, ETag-cached), `GET /status`, `GET /config` (pairing key, static peers `host[:port]`, name, this host's `addrs`, `discoveryPort`) / `PUT /config` (fully validated, persisted before hot apply; a key change drops known peers), `GET /test[?peer=…]` (TCP → discovery-authenticated TLS → pairing, plus announcements heard and sync-folder health) |
| Sync folder (`sync_dir`) | Writes `stickysites-peer-<id>.json` `{ v, id, name, ts, sig, snapshot }` (HMAC over id/name/ts/sha256(snapshot)) atomically on every snapshot change; `folder_peers()` reads the others' files (mtime/size cache), verifies the signature, and merges them into `/peers/snapshots` as `via: 'folder'`; `folder` CLI sets it live via `PUT /config`; CORS for extension origins, with loopback Host validation and no-Origin CLI support |
| LAN HTTPS `0.0.0.0:47832` | `GET /snapshot` (ETag / 304 / 204), `GET /hello`; `Authorization: Bearer HMAC(pairKey,'auth')`; self-signed cert from `openssl` |
| UDP `:47833` — multicast `239.255.77.31`, subnet broadcast, optional unicast (`static_peers`) | Announce every 5 s `{ id, name, port, fp, ts, addrs, sig }`, HMAC-signed with the pairing key, on every non-tunnel interface (table rescanned every 60 s; LAN addresses advertised first, tunnels last); listener joins the group per interface and also receives broadcasts; drops unsigned/stale/self; peers expire after 20 s |
| `fetch_peer` | Tries each announced address (recv addr first), pins the cert SHA-256 from the announcement, bearer auth, `If-None-Match` |
| CLI | `install [--pair-key] [--name] [--peer IP]` (config + cert + ad-hoc-signed `~/Applications/StickySites Peer.app` wrapper + launchd agent `com.stickysites.peer`; launches the app once so macOS can show its Local Network prompt), `uninstall`, `run`, `status`, `pair [KEY]`, `probe` (one signed announcement + bound-socket diagnostics), `folder [DIR|--clear]`, `init` (tests) |

`peer/test_peer.py` and `peer/peer_fixture.py` load actual daemon modules with isolated homes
and loopback-only dynamic HTTP/HTTPS/UDP sockets. Tests cover signed discovery, pinning,
ETags, folder transport, config/persistence failures, malformed requests, and cleanup.

## `src/shared/notes-storage.js` (ES exports) — reference CRUD; tests only

`getSiteKey`, `getPageKey`, `getDailyKey`; read/write/delete/readAll for global, site, page,
daily, todo, outline; `parseTags`; `createDebouncedSaver(fn, 500)`; `readPrefs` / `writePrefs`.
Plaintext only (no encryption). The extension runtime does not import it. Runtime mutations use the worker-owned
`note-writer.js` queue instead. This reference documents record shapes and backs
`tests/notes-storage.test.js`.

---

## Popup — `popup.html` / `popup.js` / `popup.css`

Loads settings/network, storage IPC, HTML filtering, crypto, prefs, and `popup.js` with `<script>` tags. Lock screen
(`checkAndShowLock`), Settings (Enable / Disable / Lock Now, note-type checkboxes →
`enabledTypes`, layout → `clusterLayout`, written through queued preference mutations),
`loadAllNotes()` (decrypts all six keys), search / sort / type tabs / tag filter, Markdown
export (one or all), Quick-Open row → `STICKYSITES_OPEN` to the active tab or
`STICKYSITES_POPOUT` fallback on `chrome://` pages (`computePopoutTarget`).

## Popout — `popout.html` / `popout.js` / `popout.css`

Loads shared settings/network and storage/HTML helpers, then crypto-content, note-types, prefs, todo, outline-ops, outline, mentions, panel, then
`popout.js`: reads `type`, `key`, `label` from the query string, clones the note type with
overridden `getKey` / `getLabel`, `Panel.init(window.close)`, `Panel.open`, removes the resize
grips. `popout.css` makes the panel fill the window and hides expand/popout buttons.

---

## Tooling — `scripts/`

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `check-syntax.mjs` | `npm run lint`: syntax, ESLint, and manifest ↔ package version agreement |
| `generate-docs.mjs` | `docs:generate` / `docs:check-generated`: deterministic public retrieval files from tracked sources; private bodies excluded |
| `check-doc-indexes.mjs` | `npm run docs:check-indexes`: path-validate `docs/high_signal_file_index.json` and `llms.txt` links; `--prune` |
| `rotate-workflow-logs.mjs` | `npm run logs:rotate`: move oldest `## ` sections of `memory.md` / `prompts.md` to `docs/archive/` past ~200 KB; refuses while an editor swap file is live |
| `generate-icons.js` | `npm run icons`: draw `icons/icon{16,48,128}.png` with `canvas` (CommonJS) |
| `verify-live.mjs` | `npm run verify:live`: puppeteer-core harness — identity icons, caret stability, per-page identity, SPA re-key, cross-tab sync, outliner (a–k), popup labels/storage, encryption enable/lock/unlock. Needs Chrome for Testing (`SS_CHROME`) |

Network defaults are centralized in `settings.js`: JSON requests include response-body deadlines;
native calls have a separate timeout. Daemon sockets use finite read/handshake timeouts, and
config/snapshot failures preserve the last successfully persisted state. Folder publication is
serialized and uses private unique temporary files; key/name changes invalidate publication.

## Source: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md

# Development

## Prerequisites

- A Node.js version matching `.nvmrc` and `package.json` engines for tests and tooling — the extension itself needs no Node
- Chrome or a Chromium-based browser (Edge, Brave, Arc, Chrome Beta)
- No build step: Chrome loads the repo root directly

## Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mithudso/stickysites.git && cd stickysites
npm ci               # locked development dependencies
npm run lint && npm test
```

## Loading the extension

1. `chrome://extensions` → enable **Developer mode**
2. **Load unpacked** → select the repo root
3. For an explicitly requested live smoke, click ↻ on the StickySites card
4. If `manifest.json` changed (script, permission, command): reload the extension **and**
   close/reopen the tabs you test in — Chrome does not re-inject into existing tabs
5. CSS changes in `src/content/sticky-inject.css` need a page reload on the target site

Runbook with verification steps: `runbooks/load-and-reload-extension.md`.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run lint` | Syntax checks, ESLint, and manifest/package version agreement |
| `npm test` | Vitest pure modules and actual-script runtime regressions with jsdom |
| `npm run test:peer` | Two peer daemons on ephemeral ports (Python unittest, needs `openssl`) |
| `npm run test:watch` | Watch mode |
| `npx vitest run tests/<file>` | One test file |
| `npm run docs:generate` | Regenerate public retrieval docs from tracked sources; private workflow/config bodies stay excluded |
| `npm run docs:check-generated` | Fail if generated docs differ from current sources |
| `npm run docs:check-indexes` | Validate `docs/high_signal_file_index.json` paths and `llms.txt` links; `-- --prune` drops dead entries |
| `npm run logs:rotate` | Archive old `memory.md` / `prompts.md` sections once past ~200 KB |
| `npm run icons` | Regenerate `icons/*.png` |
| `npm run verify:live` | Puppeteer end-to-end harness (`npm i --no-save puppeteer-core`; Chrome for Testing via `SS_CHROME`) |
| `npm run build:store` | Chrome Web Store zip in `dist/` (runtime files only) |
| `npm run store:screenshots` / `npm run store:promo` | Regenerate the store listing images |

CI runs the configured syntax/ESLint, Vitest, synthetic peer, documentation, package, and
manifest checks (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Do not activate the live browser, native host,
or installed daemon during automated maintenance.

## Project structure

See `codebase-overview.md` for every file. The short version:

```
src/background/service-worker.js   ES module: menus, Alt+S, popout, to-do sync
src/content/*.js                   classic scripts in manifest order → window.StickySites.*
src/content/sticky-inject.css      all injected styles
src/shared/*.js                    writer/sync/crypto ES modules; portable classic settings/network helpers
peer/                              local peer-sync daemon (Python) + its test + README
popup.* / popout.*                 extension pages
tests/                             vitest
scripts/                           lint, index check, log rotation, icons, live harness
docs/                              this documentation + runbooks + indexes
```

## Module system

Content scripts cannot `import`; each attaches to `window.StickySites`:

`Settings` → request helper → mutation IPC → HTML filter → `Crypto` → `noteTypes` →
`Prefs` → `Cluster` → `Todo` → `OutlineOps` → `Outline` → `Mentions` → `Panel` → orchestrator (`sticky-inject.js`). Adding a script means adding it to
`manifest.json` **after** its dependencies and to `popout.html` if the popout needs it.

`src/shared/note-writer.js` owns the service worker mutation queue; `storage-content.js`
sends commands to it. It reads current state and verifies writes. Native/peer sync calls
commit only while their input remains current (`STATE_CHANGED` otherwise). `settings.js`
and `network.js` are classic helpers shared with extension pages. Keep the two crypto
implementations in lock-step; `notes-storage.js` remains a plaintext test reference.

## Conventions

- **No frameworks, no build** — vanilla JS and CSS.
- **Prefix everything** injected with `stickysites-`; z-index near INT32_MAX.
- **Versioned storage keys** (`_v1`); adapt legacy shapes at read time, never bulk-migrate.
- **500 ms debounce** on auto-save; `flushPendingSave()` before close / switch / popout / re-key.
- **Snapshot the key at `open()`** — never re-derive `_activeKey` mid-session.
- **Locked vault ⇒ no plaintext writes.** Check `Crypto.getCachedKey()` before writing a note key.
- **Logging**: `console.warn('[stickysites] <subsystem>', {...})` on integration failure paths
  only; never note content or key material (`logging.md`).
- **Versions**: bump `manifest.json` and `package.json` together; log the change in
  `prompts.md` / `memory.md` (see `CLAUDE.md` → Workflow log rule).
- 2-space indent, LF, final newline (`.editorconfig`); content scripts use `var` inside the
  namespace IIFEs.

## Debugging

| Context | How |
|---|---|
| Content script | DevTools on the page → Console / Elements; look for `#stickysites-cluster`, `#stickysites-panel` |
| Service worker | `chrome://extensions` → StickySites → **Service worker**; `[stickysites]` warnings show sync/tab failures |
| Popup / popout | Right-click the page → Inspect |
| Storage | any extension console: `chrome.storage.local.get(null, console.log)` |
| Encryption state | `chrome.storage.local.get(['stickysites_crypto_v1','stickysites_cached_key'], console.log)` — a JWK under `stickysites_cached_key` means unlocked |
| To-do sync | `runbooks/todo-sync-troubleshooting.md` |
| Peer sync | popup → Settings → Local Peer Sync status; `python3 peer/stickysites-peer.py status`; `~/.stickysites/peer.log`; `runbooks/peer-sync.md` |

Encrypted storage values appear as `{ iv, data }` envelopes instead of records.

## Packaging

`runbooks/release-packaging.md` — version bump, tag, store zip, rollback.

## Source: docs/INSTALLATION.md

# Installation

## Developer install (from source)

### Prerequisites

- Chrome or a Chromium-based browser (Edge, Brave, Arc, Chrome Beta) with Manifest V3 support
- Git
- Node.js matching `.nvmrc` and `package.json` engines — only for tests and tooling

### Steps

1. Clone:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/mithudso/stickysites.git
   cd stickysites
   ```
2. (Optional, tests/tooling) `npm ci && npm run lint && npm test`
3. Load: `chrome://extensions` → **Developer mode** on → **Load unpacked** → select the
   `stickysites/` directory (the one containing `manifest.json`)
4. Verify: the StickySites icon appears in the toolbar; on any `http(s)` page a floating
   cluster of colored icons appears (default top-right). Click one, or press `Ctrl/Cmd+F1`,
   to open a note. `Alt+S` hides/shows the cluster.

### Optional: to-do sync with a local `TODO.md`

The global to-do list can mirror into a Markdown file through a native-messaging host that
lives outside this repo (`~/.claude/skills/todo/`). Install it for every browser profile:

```bash
python3 ~/.claude/skills/todo/scripts/todo.py install-native-host
```

Then reload the extension. Without the host the extension works normally and the list stays
in the browser. Troubleshooting: `runbooks/todo-sync-troubleshooting.md`.

### Optional: keep two laptops in sync over the local network

Install the peer helper on each machine with the same pairing key (`peer/README.md`):

```bash
python3 peer/stickysites-peer.py install                 # first laptop — prints the key
python3 peer/stickysites-peer.py install --pair-key KEY  # the others
```

Then enable Local Peer Sync in popup Settings and use **Sync now**. A user-selected
shared/cloud folder is an alternative to direct LAN transport; your provider then stores
and transfers the snapshot files. See `peer/README.md` for security and setup.

### Updating

```bash
git pull
```
then `chrome://extensions` → ↻ on the StickySites card. If `manifest.json` changed, also
close and reopen the tabs you use.

### Uninstall

- `chrome://extensions` → **Remove** on the StickySites card (this deletes the extension's
  `chrome.storage.local`, i.e. all notes — export first from the popup if you want them)
- If installed, `python3 peer/stickysites-peer.py uninstall` removes the helper job. It
  retains `~/.stickysites/`; clear any shared-folder files separately if you want to purge them.
- Delete the cloned directory
- If installed, remove the native host manifest
  `~/Library/Application Support/<Browser>/NativeMessagingHosts/com.mitch.todo_bridge.json`

## Chrome Web Store

Not yet published. Submission kit (assets, copy, checklist): `store/README.md`; packaging: `runbooks/release-packaging.md`.

## Source: docs/MCP.md

# MCP

## Shipped runtime

StickySites ships no Model Context Protocol server or MCP operation registry. Its runtime is
an extension plus an optional Python peer daemon/CLI. The optional native host is installed
outside this repository. Native, loopback, paired LAN, and shared-folder boundaries are
inventoried in [external-calls.md](external-calls.md).

## Developer tooling

`global_ai_hub` is a machine-wide developer tool configured by `.mcp.json` and
`.vscode/mcp.json`. It supplies semantic search (`hub_search_codebase`,
`hub_search_symbols`, `hub_ask`) and project lookup (`hub_pm_get`). It is not shipped with
the extension, and the build/tests do not depend on it. There is no repo-local indexer.
Use the tool's actual schema for search filters; do not invent a `--prefix` argument.
If the hub is unavailable, use `rg` and read the source.

## Project record maintenance

Use the installed `project_manager.py` CLI, after inspecting its help. Read the existing
record before an update:

```bash
python3 "$HOME/.global-ai-hub/scripts/project_manager.py" get stickysites
python3 "$HOME/.global-ai-hub/scripts/project_manager.py" upsert stickysites --path "$PWD" --status <existing-status>
```

Replace `<existing-status>` with the status just read. The CLI defaults to `active`; omitting
`--status` can overwrite a preserved status. Do not initialize, delete, or recreate the hub
registry to refresh this repository's path. Hub authentication/endpoints remain machine
configuration outside the public repository.

## Source: docs/SECURITY.md

# Security

## Threat model

StickySites runs as a Chrome Extension on every web page. It injects DOM into untrusted host
pages, stores user notes locally with optional encryption, and (optionally) exchanges the
to-do list with a local native-messaging host. An optional daemon exposes loopback HTTP
and authenticated LAN HTTPS/UDP discovery, and can use a shared/cloud folder.

### Attack surface

| Vector | Risk | Mitigation |
|--------|------|------------|
| Host page reads note content from the injected DOM | Medium — page JS can query `#stickysites-panel` while it is open | Encryption protects data at rest only; in-memory plaintext is exposed while a panel is open on that page. Future: Shadow DOM (`known-issues.md`). |
| Host page spoofs `#stickysites-cluster` to suppress injection | Low | Denial of the UI only; no data exposure. |
| XSS via note content | Low — notes are user-authored rich HTML rendered in a `contenteditable` | Imported/synced rich HTML is parsed inertly and filtered by `safe-html.js` before live rendering. Scripts, event attributes, resource nodes, and unsafe URLs are removed. Clipped text is escaped. This does not isolate the open panel from host scripts. |
| Storage tampering by another extension | Low | `chrome.storage.local` is isolated per extension. |
| Cached key on disk | Medium while unlocked | `stickysites_cached_key` (JWK) sits in the Chrome profile until **Lock Now**. Anyone with the profile directory and the extension id can read it. Lock when leaving the machine; see the encryption runbook. |
| Host page reads an unlock passphrase | Prevented by origin separation | Page notices request a fixed extension-origin popup; passphrases are entered only there, not in injected page inputs. |
| Passphrase brute force against the stored `verify` envelope | Low | PBKDF2 600,000 iterations, SHA-256, random 16-byte salt. |
| Native host impersonation | Low | Chrome only launches the host registered in the browser's `NativeMessagingHosts` manifest whose `allowed_origins` contains this extension id; the host runs as the local user. |
| Plaintext to-dos reaching `TODO.md` | By design when encryption is off | Sync is skipped entirely while `stickysites_todos_v1` is an encrypted envelope. |
| Peer daemon loopback API abused by another local extension | Low–Medium | Bound to `127.0.0.1`, validates loopback Host and extension Origin; cross-site browser GETs are rejected; no-Origin CLI requests remain supported; any extension on that machine could read/replace the snapshot — same trust boundary as the Chrome profile. Vault on ⇒ note buckets are envelopes; metadata remains readable. |
| Stranger on the LAN joins the sync | Low | Announcements are HMAC-signed with the pairing key and dropped otherwise; LAN requests need a bearer token derived from it; TLS cert fingerprint pinned from the signed announcement. Rotate the key with `stickysites-peer.py pair`. |
| Notes readable on the Wi-Fi | Low | Peer transport is HTTPS with pinned certs. Without the vault, notes are plaintext inside the tunnel; tombstones (record keys + timestamps) are always plaintext. |
| Snapshot file at rest | Same as Chrome storage | `~/.stickysites/snapshot.json` mode 0600; envelopes when the vault is on. |
| Shared/cloud-folder snapshot | Provider and local account can read plaintext metadata, and notes when the vault is off | HMAC authenticates files without encrypting them; choose the folder/provider deliberately and enable the vault for note confidentiality. |
| Stalled LAN client | Worker resource use | TLS handshakes run in workers with finite socket timeouts, leaving acceptance available. |
| Content script on sensitive pages | N/A | Chrome blocks content scripts on `chrome://`, `chrome-extension://`, the Web Store. |

### Permissions audit

| Permission | Justification | Least privilege? |
|------------|--------------|------------------|
| `storage` | Notes, prefs, crypto config, cached key in `chrome.storage.local` | Yes |
| `activeTab` | Message the active tab from the SW and popup | Yes — no broad host access |
| `contextMenus` | The "StickySites" clip submenu | Yes |
| `alarms` | To-do and peer sync schedules | Yes |
| `nativeMessaging` | Local IPC with `com.mitch.todo_bridge`; only a host manifest naming this extension id can answer | Yes — no network |

No `tabs`, `webRequest`, `cookies`, `history`, `identity`, `scripting`, or extra host permissions.

### Data handling

- Notes live in `chrome.storage.local` by default. No hosted telemetry, crash reporting,
  remote scripts, or remote resources are loaded.
- Optional native messaging sends plaintext to-dos to a local file while encryption is off.
- Optional loopback requests hand snapshots to the local daemon. The daemon can relay them
  to paired LAN machines or write signed files to a user-selected shared/cloud folder. The
  selected provider may store and transfer those files outside the LAN.
- Vault encryption covers the six note buckets. Tombstones (record keys/timestamps), crypto
  config, device identities, and folder-envelope metadata remain plaintext. Folder signatures
  authenticate snapshots; they do not encrypt them.

## Encryption at rest

Opt-in; enabled from the popup Settings panel with a passphrase.

### Algorithm

- **Cipher**: AES-256-GCM (confidentiality + integrity), 12-byte random IV per operation.
- **KDF**: PBKDF2, 600,000 iterations, SHA-256, random 16-byte salt.
- **Envelope**: `{ iv: base64, data: base64 }`. `isEncrypted()` accepts only that shape and
  rejects objects with `body`, `items`, or `siteKey` so a plain record is never mistaken for
  an envelope.

### Key lifecycle

1. `enable(passphrase)` derives a key and stages all encrypted note buckets, the verify
   token, configuration, and cached JWK before one guarded multi-key commit. A staging failure
   leaves the prior state intact. The passphrase is never stored.
2. Reads: `decryptValue()` uses the cached key; if none, the value stays an envelope and the UI
   shows the lock overlay (or the outliner's lock notice).
3. **Lock Now** (popup) / `clearCachedKey()`: clears the JWK value in `stickysites_cached_key` and the
   in-memory key. The cached key otherwise **persists across browser restarts**.
4. `unlock(passphrase)`: re-derive from the stored salt, decrypt `verify`, compare; on success
   cache the key again.
5. `disable()` stages every decryption before one guarded commit of plaintext buckets and
   cleared config/key. An unreadable bucket preserves the existing vault for recovery.

If a content page lacks `crypto.subtle` (ordinary HTTP), the content namespace routes vault
operations to the extension worker. The worker runs the same lifecycle implementation and
returns results over extension IPC. This preserves the envelope and local-JWK design.
See [MDN secure-context restrictions](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/Content_scripts#secure_contexts).

### Invariants the code enforces

- Never write plaintext to a note key while enabled and no cached key: the outliner shows a
  lock notice instead of auto-creating; the to-do sync skips; `syncFromStorage` skips; peer
  sync reports `locked` and writes nothing.
- Peer sync never mixes vaults: same salt → merge on decrypted data and re-encrypt; different
  salts → `mismatch`, nothing written; local vault off + peer on → adopt the peer's config
  (salt + verify token, never the passphrase) and lock.
- `src/content/crypto-content.js` and `src/shared/crypto.js` implement the same primitives
  and must change together.

### Mutation and transport boundaries

All runtime mutations enter the service worker queue, read fresh records, and verify the
stored result. Native/peer results commit only if their original inputs still match;
`STATE_CHANGED` preserves newer edits. This is a single-extension coordination mechanism,
not a filesystem or database transaction against unrelated programs.

The daemon validates request lengths before reading and bounds body/handshake waits.
Diagnostic requests send a bearer only after the remote certificate matches authenticated
discovery. Unknown certificates stop at the TLS step. Config and snapshot disk failures
preserve the prior successful state.

### Caveats

- Encryption covers the six note keys only; prefs, tombstones, and crypto/sync metadata are plaintext.
- There is no passphrase recovery; losing it means losing the notes
  (`runbooks/encryption-lock-and-recovery.md`).
- PBKDF2 at 600 K iterations takes 1–4 s on slow hardware with no spinner.

## Reporting vulnerabilities

See [`.github/SECURITY.md`](../.github/SECURITY.md): private advisory or maintainer email,
acknowledgement within 3 business days, fix or plan within 14 days.

## Source: docs/TESTING.md

# Testing

## Commands

Use the Node version in `.nvmrc` that satisfies `package.json` engines, then `npm ci`.

```bash
npm run lint                              # syntax, ESLint, manifest/package version agreement
npm test                                  # Vitest pure modules and runtime regressions
npm run test:peer                         # Python/OpenSSL; isolated actual daemon modules
npm run test:watch                        # Vitest watch mode
npx vitest run tests/todo-bridge.test.js   # focused file
npm run docs:check-indexes                # retrieval/wiki paths resolve
npm run docs:check-generated             # generated docs agree with sources
npm run build:store                       # runtime package validation
```

CI runs JavaScript and peer tests inside a Linux network namespace with only loopback.
Package installation occurs before that isolation.

CI's exact gates are in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Test totals and source line counts are
not documentation contracts; inspect the current runner output. Passing synthetic tests does
not establish a live browser, installed native host, launchd job, or real LAN deployment.

## Suites and fixtures

| File/group | Coverage |
|---|---|
| `notes-storage.test.js` | Reference CRUD, keys, timestamps, tags, and preference shapes |
| `outline-ops.test.js` | Tree operations, filtering, tags, grouping, Markdown/OPML export |
| `crypto.test.js` | Salt/key derivation, AES-GCM round trips, wrong-key rejection, envelope shapes |
| `peer-sync.test.js` | Snapshot shape, vault compatibility, record LWW, tombstones, orchestration |
| `todo-bridge.test.js` | Native request/reply normalization, local-only fields, encrypted skip, failures |
| `ui-boundaries.test.js` | Save/blur/transition races, outline clips, checkbox/formatting persistence, OPML whitespace, popout lock, cluster geometry |
| `runtime-regressions.test.js` | Actual classic-script rendering, mentions, HTML filtering, queued mutations, vault staging, and stale/failed writes |
| `popup-regressions.test.js` | Actual popup lock/settings behavior, preference merging, stale async work, bounded response bodies |
| `browser-integration.test.js`, `service-worker.test.js` | Manifest script order, all six editors, clip/vault/lock, actual worker alarm/message completion |
| `vault-legacy.test.js`, `vault-import.test.js` | Always-on frozen-corpus decryption; optional-package absence versus installed import failure |
| `sync-regressions.test.js` | Changes during native/peer requests, malformed peers, response-body deadlines |
| `tooling*.test.js` | Package, syntax, documentation generation, and optional browser-harness behavior |
| `peer/test_peer.py`, `peer/peer_fixture.py` | Actual daemon discovery, handlers, pinned TLS, auth, ETags, folder/config/persistence failures, invalid lengths, stalled clients, fixture cleanup/isolation |
| `crypto-vault-compat.test.js` | Optional private-package interoperability against frozen legacy envelopes; package absence skips this suite |

`tests/helpers/runtime.js` uses jsdom and synthetic Chrome storage/IPC. Tests load the actual
classic scripts rather than a rewritten implementation. Worker tests also simulate an HTTP
content context without WebCrypto and assert asynchronous response channels remain open. Storage, native replies, and fetch
responses remain synthetic. Tests do not activate the user's extension, daemon, or host.

The Python fixture imports fresh daemon modules with temporary `STICKYSITES_HOME` directories
and dynamic ports. HTTP, HTTPS, and UDP sockets bind to `127.0.0.1`. It keeps production HMAC
announce/listen logic while directing discovery over loopback unicast with a synthetic
interface inventory. It exercises the same server factory as `run()`, registers cleanup
before acquisition, retains bounded startup diagnostics, and supports concurrent runs without
LAN permissions or fixed ports. Python 3.9+ and `openssl` are required.

For this maintenance batch, local automated tests use the task-local process-tree egress
runner outside this repository. It denies outbound traffic, including loopback, except exact
owned TCP fixture ports. The peer guarded launcher reserves and inherits those listeners.
The runner cannot permit UDP fixture sends. Local guarded parser tests use an injected
datagram socket; the full actual UDP discovery test runs in isolated CI. Earlier local
loopback passes preceded the guard and are not evidence of guarded isolation. Git test
fixtures strip inherited selectors/config, use empty templates, and verify effective hooks
before committing; a hostile hook sentinel checks that boundary.

## Compatibility boundaries

`tests/fixtures/legacy-crypto-envelopes.json` is a frozen historical corpus. Normal tests do
not regenerate it or install the optional private package. A skipped private compatibility
suite is not evidence of interoperability. Follow the suite's setup instructions only when
that private-package work is explicitly in scope.

## Coverage target and limits

Prioritize observable data-loss, stale-write, vault, import/rendering, and integration failure
paths. Add a behavioral regression when changing those contracts. No blanket line-percentage
threshold is enforced. Use `vi.spyOn(console, 'warn')` when the log behavior matters.

jsdom cannot establish real `execCommand`, caret/layout, extension permission handling,
Chrome service-worker lifecycle, or OS network authorization. The synthetic peer suite does
not establish real multicast/broadcast delivery, VPN behavior, cloud-client propagation, or
launchd installation. Keep these limits in verification reports.

## Optional live harnesses

`npm run verify:live` and `npm run store:screenshots` use puppeteer-core and a compatible
Chrome for Testing/Chromium binary. Install the optional harness prerequisite only when a
live run is authorized; set `SS_CHROME` for either harness. Branded Chrome versions may
ignore `--load-extension`; consult the current harness prerequisites.

The verification harness serves local fixtures and checks identity icons, caret stability,
page identity, SPA navigation, cross-tab sync, outliner interactions, popup storage, and
vault enable/lock/unlock. Screenshots go to `/tmp/stickysites-verify`. Store screenshots have
their own output under `store/screenshots/`. Neither harness's presence proves it was run.
Do not reload an active user extension or daemon merely to complete automated maintenance.
For an explicitly requested manual smoke, follow
[load/reload](runbooks/load-and-reload-extension.md).

## Source: docs/caching-and-optimization.md

# Caching and Optimization

## Cache layers

| Layer | What is cached | Invalidation |
|---|---|---|
| `Crypto._cachedKey` (in-memory, per page / per extension page) | The imported `CryptoKey` after the first `getCachedKey()` | Cleared by `clearCachedKey()` (Lock Now, disable) and on page unload |
| `chrome.storage.local["stickysites_cached_key"]` | JWK export of the derived AES-GCM key | Removed by Lock Now / disable; **persists across browser restarts** until then |
| `Panel._loadedIds` | Ids of to-do items present when the panel opened | Rebuilt on every `open()`; lets `_writeStructured` keep items another writer (the TODO.md sync) added meanwhile |
| `Panel._lastWrittenBody` | The HTML this panel last saved | Used by `syncFromStorage` to skip its own echo from `chrome.storage.onChanged` |
| Daemon peer ETags | Last fetched snapshot per authenticated peer | A changed ETag fetches fresh content; pairing-key rotation clears trust/cache |
| Daemon folder cache | File docs keyed by mtime and size; last published snapshot etag | Folder/key/name changes invalidate publication; writes serialize with signing config |
| Popup `loadAllNotes()` result | Decrypted list of every note | Re-read on every popup open; no persistence |

The extension has no CDN or hosted database. It stores data in `chrome.storage.local`;
the optional daemon also stores a local snapshot and uses peer HTTP ETags/folder caches.

## Performance patterns in use

- **Debounced auto-save (500 ms)** for every editor (`panel.js`); `flushPendingSave()` forces
  the trailing write before close / switch / popout / SPA re-key.
- **Debounced to-do sync (3 s)** after a `stickysites_todos_v1` change, plus a 2-minute
  `chrome.alarms` period, with a `todoSyncRunning` re-entrancy guard (`service-worker.js`).
- **Change detection before write** in `todo-bridge.applyHostResult` — a canonical
  (key-sorted) serialization compares the merged list with the stored one so unchanged
  syncs never touch storage or wake other tabs.
- **Read-time schema adaptation** instead of migrations: legacy `siteKey`/`pageKey`/hostname
  outline keys are normalised when read, never rewritten in bulk.
- **1 s `href` poll** for SPA navigation (`sticky-inject.js`) instead of a `MutationObserver`
  over the whole document.
- **`document_idle`** injection so the host page finishes its own work first.
- **Single `chrome.storage.onChanged` listener** per tab fans out to the open panel only.

## Known bottlenecks

| Bottleneck | Cost | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| PBKDF2 at 600,000 iterations | 1–4 s per unlock on slow hardware, blocks the unlock button | Deliberate KDF cost; a spinner is an open item in `known-issues.md` |
| `enable()` / `disable()` re-encrypt all six note keys in one pass | Proportional to total note size | Stages all bucket transformations before one guarded commit; a failed stage preserves prior state |
| Popup `loadAllNotes()` decrypts every record on open | Linear in note count | Acceptable at hundreds of notes; paginate if it grows |
| `execCommand`-based toolbar | Synchronous DOM mutation on large bodies | No action; bodies are small |

## Profiling

- **Content script**: DevTools → Performance on the host page; filter by `stickysites` in the
  call tree. Record while typing to see the 500 ms save cadence.
- **Service worker**: `chrome://extensions` → Service worker → Performance tab; trigger a
  sync by editing a to-do and watch `runTodoSync`.
- **Storage size**: in any extension console,
  `chrome.storage.local.getBytesInUse(null, b => console.log(b))`.

## Source: docs/external-calls.md

# External Calls

StickySites operates no hosted service or telemetry. Optional native and loopback calls leave
the browser. The peer daemon can then use a paired LAN or a user-selected shared/cloud folder;
a cloud provider may transfer files outside the LAN. Browser APIs such as storage, tabs,
windows, alarms, and context menus are inventoried in `integrations-and-assumptions.md`.

## Inventory

| Boundary | Call and implementation | Trigger | Authentication and bounds | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Local native host | `sendNativeMessage(TODO_HOST, {cmd:'sync', ext, items, sections})`; `todo-bridge.js`, SW `runTodoSync` | Startup/install, two-minute alarm, three-second edit debounce | Host `com.mitch.todo_bridge`, browser manifest `allowed_origins`; native deadline in `settings.js` | Synthetic bridge/sync tests; guarded commit and persisted-value verification |
| Loopback daemon | SW `PUT /snapshot`, `GET /peers/snapshots`; popup status/config/test calls; `peer-sync.js`, `network.js`, `popup.js` | Startup/install, minute alarm, four-second edit debounce, popup controls | `127.0.0.1:47831`; daemon Host/Origin validation; fetch/JSON-body deadlines | Actual-script popup/sync tests plus isolated actual-daemon tests |
| Paired LAN | Daemon signed UDP discovery on port 47833 and HTTPS snapshots on port 47832 | Five-second announcements; peer fetches | HMAC pairing key, bearer, fingerprint pin from signed discovery; finite socket timeouts | Synthetic loopback unicast discovery and pinned TLS; real LAN authorization/delivery remains a live check |
| Shared/cloud folder | Daemon writes/reads `stickysites-peer-<id>.json` in `sync_dir` | Snapshot publication and peer reads | HMAC file signatures; private unique temporary files and serialized atomic replacement | Synthetic folder, key-rotation, malformed-file, concurrent-write, and persistence tests |

## Native host data and outcomes

The host receives item `id`, `text`, `done`, `note`, `section`; section `id`/`name`; and the
extension id. The reply contains merged items with section names. Native sync reattaches
StickySites-only fields rather than sending them through this native boundary. Peer snapshots
separately include the full stored note buckets. Native sync skips while the vault is enabled
or the to-do value is encrypted. A stale reply is rejected with `STATE_CHANGED`.

Install instructions and the optional live troubleshooting steps are in
[the to-do runbook](runbooks/todo-sync-troubleshooting.md). Normal tests use no installed host.

| Outcome | Meaning and action |
|---|---|
| `skipped: encrypted` | Vault prevents plaintext native-file export |
| Native host missing/forbidden | Install the host for this browser/extension id if wanted; otherwise notes remain local |
| Malformed/no reply or `NATIVE_TIMEOUT` | Preserve the current list; inspect the host if sync is expected |
| `STATE_CHANGED` | Input changed during the call; preserve newer edits and let a later scheduled run retry |
| Storage read/write or `STORAGE_VERIFY_FAILED` | Persistence did not complete or verify; inspect the reported failure |
| `changed: false` / `changed: true` | No mutation needed / verified mutation completed |

## Peer snapshots and outcomes

Snapshots contain the six note buckets, tombstones, device identity, and vault configuration.
Preferences and the cached key do not sync. Vault-on note buckets are encrypted envelopes;
tombstone keys/timestamps, crypto configuration, and device/folder metadata remain plaintext.
Vault-off snapshots contain plaintext notes. A folder signature authenticates the file and
does not encrypt it. See [privacy](../PRIVACY.md) and [peer setup](../peer/README.md).

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `no-daemon` | Loopback connection failed; one warning per outage; later alarm retries |
| `no-peers` | No usable other snapshot seen |
| `unreachable` / `partial` | Discovered peer errors prevent all/some fetches; inspect per-peer errors |
| `ok` | Merge completed; status includes changed keys and applied/deleted/kept counts |
| `locked` | Unlock before merging |
| `adopted-remote-vault` | Peer config adopted; enter that vault's passphrase |
| `mismatch` | Different vault salts; reconcile deliberately using the peer runbook |
| `error` | Bounded request, decryption, stale input, or persistence failure; current data is retained on rejected commits |
| `disabled` | User toggle is off |

Network work stays outside the service worker write queue. A guarded commit checks its input
before publishing a result; verification reads the persisted values. Scheduled retries are
bounded by the normal alarms rather than an unbounded in-process loop. The daemon keeps the
last successful config/snapshot when disk replacement fails.

## Standards applicability

The extension has no hosted operations registry or dashboard runtime. It does have an optional
peer CLI, popup sync/status controls, browser-console diagnostics, and a daemon file log at
`~/.stickysites/peer.log`. These are the actual operational surfaces; inventing `tam_ops_*`
MCP tools would add a different product. The historical five-standard assessment and its
2026-09-27 retractions remain in `repo-bootstrap-audit-2026-09-27.md`; current runtime behavior
above supersedes its old "no read-back" and missing-status descriptions.

## Development and daemon administration boundaries

These commands are explicit developer actions. CI and the synthetic tests do not install,
reload, sign, or start an installed application. File writes stay at the documented output
paths. A failed verification does not imply that a previous write was rolled back.

| Implementation | Target and trigger | Failure log / policy | Test or verification / docs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scripts/check-syntax.mjs:36` | Child Node `--check` for each maintained JS file; `npm run lint` | Named file/error, nonzero exit; fix then rerun | `tests/tooling.test.js`; DEVELOPMENT |
| `scripts/generate-docs.mjs`, `execFileSync` | Read-only `git ls-files`; text files written by `npm run docs:generate` | Named generation error/nonzero; `--check` reads only; rerun after fixing | `tests/tooling-docs.test.js`, generated drift gate; DEVELOPMENT |
| `scripts/build-store-zip.mjs:51` | Child `zip` and `unzip`; `npm run build:store` | Nonzero on subprocess or membership failure; rejected artifact removed; manual retry | `tests/tooling.test.js`; release-packaging runbook |
| `scripts/harness-resources.mjs`; `verify-live.mjs`, `store-screenshots.mjs` | Explicit Chrome-for-Testing launch, local fixture HTTP server, screenshots/downloads | Privacy-safe step/cleanup error; no automatic live run; owned resources cleaned in finally, profiles retained if browser cannot close | `tests/tooling-harness.test.js`; TESTING and release-packaging runbook |
| `scripts/generate-icons.js`, `store-promo.mjs` | Canvas raster files in `icons/` or `store/promo/`; explicit npm commands | CLI error/nonzero; inspect output then rerun | Source audit and existing generated assets only; no regeneration claimed; release-packaging runbook |
| `scripts/rotate-workflow-logs.mjs` | Repository logs/archive plus private Git-state journal/lock; `npm run logs:rotate` | Named failure, preserve unresolved journal; explicit dead-owner `--recover`; no blanket retry | `tests/tooling.test.js`; logging guide |
| `peer/stickysites-peer.py`, `ensure_cert` | Child OpenSSL creates a local self-signed certificate during explicit initialization | Checked subprocess failure; correct local prerequisites before retry | Disposable actual-daemon fixture; peer README |
| `peer/stickysites-peer.py`, `local_ipv4_interfaces` / `_ifname_for` | `ip`, `ifconfig`, hostname resolution, UDP route selection | Bounded commands/fallback addresses; discovery retries on its normal schedule | Source audit; synthetic fixtures override interfaces to loopback; real OS/LAN routing not verified |
| `peer/stickysites-peer.py`, `install` / `uninstall` / app wrapper | Explicit CLI writes app/plist and invokes Apple Python probe, `codesign`, `launchctl`, `open` | CLI errors; inspect local install/status before manual action | Source audit only; never executed in maintenance; peer README |
